description: Phase 2 parity: after Enter (and, on a fresh instance, Cmd-C) copies the captured URI, the Copied confirmation shows, the panel stays up with it for at least ~1 s, then hides by itself within ~3 s of the key (state, window_id and Quartz all agree), and the pasteboard holds the URI
requirement: P2-copy-dismiss (GPUI Phase 2 parity, Tauri dist/panel.js confirmCopy: copy, then dismiss_panel)
notes: Tauri dismisses straight after copying (U2: done in two actions, get out of the way). The README contract adds that the Copied Label stays visible at least 1 s before a self-dismiss, so a user sees the confirmation; copy-link.json (Copied visible after the key, pasteboard read) stays valid alongside this.

Timing: the Copied node is awaited, then the pasteboard is read, then sleep 700 ms; with the a11y poll and the steps' own overhead the visibility check lands at about 1 s after the key. It is deliberately a little under 1 s so a correct implementation that hides at exactly 1.0 s is not flaky. Implementations should hold the confirmation about 1.2-1.5 s.
'Hides within 3 s' is measured from the key press and is approximate: the hidden check retries for 2000 ms after the ~1 s visible check, so the panel must be gone about 3 s after the key.
Hidden means three things (panel-dismiss.json): state.shell.visible false and route null, window_id refuses (no panel), and the window number winframe recorded is gone from Quartz's on-screen list.
The Cmd-C round runs after a restart so it does not depend on the Enter round's dismissal.
Each round is a block: if another app steals focus during a visibility check, the probe re-runs the round once from a closed panel.
